name: Bright Lilac
lede: Bright Lilac is a vivid pale purple drawn from a Crayola crayon of the same name, also recorded independently by the 2010 xkcd survey.

sections.title: Two lists, one color
sections.body:
Wikipedia's "List of colors" entry for this shade cites the Crayola crayon of the same name as its source, and the 2010 xkcd survey separately recorded its own cluster at this hue, under its own crowd-chosen label [1]. The name itself follows ordinary modifier grammar, "bright" in front of the base color [[lilac]] [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[light-amparo-purple]], [[baby-purple]], [[lavender-pink]] and [[vivid-lilac]], at 3.9, 4.5, 5.3 and 5.6 ΔE [1]. Family neighbors are [[lilac]], [[lavender]], [[purple]], and [[magenta]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, has no painting where this bright violet-pink covers five percent or more of the canvas [2]. Lilac-family pigments bright enough to reach this saturation at this lightness are a modern development; nothing in the archive's older material gets close [2].
